items.item: The external-memory model charges one unit per block transfer and treats computation on data already in the fast level as free

at.step: The model: Aggarwal and Vitter, 1988

items.item: N, M and B are counted in items, not bytes, and the model requires M < N and at least two blocks to fit in memory at once (B <= M/2)

at.step: Three numbers describe the job

items.item: A scan costs Theta(N/B) transfers and is the floor for any computation that must look at all the data

at.step: A scan touches every block once

items.item: A sorted search costs Theta(log base B of N) transfers rather than Theta(log base 2 of N), because one block transfer rules out a 1/B share of the range

at.step: Search costs log base B, not log base two

items.item: The sort bound's logarithm is a count of merge passes: run formation makes N/M runs, and each merge pass folds the run count by the fan-in M/B

at.step: Predict: how many passes to sort it?
The sort bound is a pass count

items.item: Because the fan-in is typically in the thousands, almost every realistic external sort finishes in two or three passes regardless of data size, until the run count first exceeds the fan-in

at.step: Predict: does it stay two passes forever?

items.item: Random access to N items costs about N block transfers (one per item), B times worse than sorting the same items first and scanning them, which is why engines sort or partition before probing one at a time

at.step: Predict: lookups vs sort-then-scan

items.item: Counted in block transfers, a sort that needs billions of comparisons in the word-RAM model needs only a few hundred thousand transfers, and real wall-clock time tracks the transfer count

at.step: Count the same sort twice

items.item: The doubling vector's amortized O(1) element-write bound becomes O(1/B) amortized block transfers once resizes are counted as scans, a strictly stronger result under the same proof

at.step: Repricing the doubling vector

items.item: The same two-parameter model applies at every boundary of the memory hierarchy; only M and B change, for example B = 8 keys at a 64-byte cache line versus B = 512 keys at a disk page

at.step: The same model at every boundary

items.item: The I/O model predicts the shape of a cost (its growth and pass structure) but not the constant; device latency, bandwidth, caching and prefetching set the constant and must be measured

at.step: The honest caveat: measure the constant
